title: Supported closed-unit construction and normalization of scalar comparison
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme with complementary closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ and quasi-compact open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $A_X\to B_X$ be a map of commutative ring sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; all rings on $Z,U$ are their inverse images. On ordinary unbounded module derived categories use $T_V=B_V\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_V}-$ and the canonical scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Suppose the open/closed functors and actual adjunction maps satisfy the conclusions of [lem-sfb-exact-open-closed-unbounded-calculus], and use the specified inverse-image comparisons $\theta_i,\theta_j$ of [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. For $M\in D(Z,A_Z)$ put $H=T_Xi_{*,A}M$. With closed unit $\eta_B:1\to i_{*,B}i_B^*$ and counits $\varepsilon_R:i_R^*i_{*,R}\to1$, the natural $B_X$-linear morphism
$$\delta_M=i_{*,B}T_Z(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ i_{*,B}(\theta_{i,i_{*,A}M}^{-1})\circ\eta_{B,H}:H\longrightarrow i_{*,B}T_ZM$$
is invertible. It has zero open restriction and satisfies the precise normalization
$$\varepsilon_{B,T_ZM}\circ i_B^*(\delta_M)=T_Z(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ\theta_{i,i_{*,A}M}^{-1}.$$
It is the unique morphism with this normalization. This is a formula and uniqueness statement for the supported-unit construction, with the new coefficient action retained.

proof.text: Write $Q_R=i_R^*$, $I_R=i_{*,R}$ and $P_R=j_R^*$. The assumed unbounded calculus gives $P_AI_A=0$ and $P_BI_B=0$. The specified open scalar comparison gives $P_BH\cong T_UP_AI_AM\cong T_U0$. Here $T_U0\cong0$: by the scalar adjunction, for every $N$, $\operatorname{Hom}(T_U0,N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(0,\operatorname{Res}N)$ is a singleton, so $T_U0$ is initial, hence is a zero object of the derived category. Thus $P_BH=0$, and also $P_BI_BT_ZM=0$. This establishes support for both objects without a boundedness or flatness assumption.

source.place: (1)-(2), inverse-image scalar comparison and support of the closed extension

proof.text: The assumed calculus now makes $\eta_{B,H}:H\to I_BQ_BH$ invertible, and makes $\varepsilon_{A,M}:Q_AI_AM\to M$ invertible. Put $N=T_ZM$ and $\alpha_M=T_Z(\varepsilon_{A,M})\circ\theta_{i,I_AM}^{-1}:Q_BH\to N$. The scalar-comparison lemma makes $\theta_i$ invertible; functors preserve inverses, so $\alpha_M$ is invertible. Therefore $\delta_M=I_B(\alpha_M)\circ\eta_{B,H}$ is a composite of isomorphisms and equals exactly the displayed formula in the statement. Each factor is a morphism in a derived category of $B$-modules, so the construction retains the $B_X$-action. Each factor is natural in $M$ (unit, counit, inverse of the natural comparison, and functor application); composing their naturality squares proves naturality of $\delta$. By step 1 its open restriction is the unique morphism between zero objects, hence zero.

source.place: (2), closed-unit comparison, coefficient action and invertibility

proof.text:
Use the actual $Q_B\dashv I_B$ from the calculus. Naturality of its counit applied to $\alpha_M:Q_BH\to N$, followed by its left triangle identity, gives
$$\varepsilon_{B,N}\circ Q_B(\delta_M)=\varepsilon_{B,N}\circ Q_BI_B(\alpha_M)\circ Q_B(\eta_{B,H})=\alpha_M\circ\varepsilon_{B,Q_BH}\circ Q_B(\eta_{B,H})=\alpha_M.$$
Substituting the definition of $\alpha_M$ proves precisely the asserted normalization; no unnamed comparison between adjunction maps has been inserted.

source.place: (2), restriction normalization of the closed-unit comparison

proof.text:
For any morphism $f:H\to I_BN$, naturality of the unit and the right triangle identity of the same adjunction give
$$I_B(\varepsilon_{B,N}\circ Q_Bf)\circ\eta_{B,H}=I_B(\varepsilon_{B,N})\circ\eta_{B,I_BN}\circ f=f.$$
If $f$ has the required normalization, its left side is $I_B(\alpha_M)\circ\eta_{B,H}=\delta_M$. Hence $f=\delta_M$. This proves uniqueness among all morphisms with the given source and target, and in particular uniqueness among the natural $B$-linear comparisons.

source.place: (2), uniqueness for the specified restriction normalization
